line: pg shard concurrency (no is_parallel: false anywhere)
summary: All pg shards (A/B/D/E/C) run CONCURRENTLY against a SINGLE shared Postgres instance per CI runner (per-agent-index #2094, not per-shard) -- splitting a shard reduces ITS OWN tail latency but not the aggregate WAL/fsync-heavy CREATE/DROP DATABASE load on the one shared instance. Real CI evidence (run 32004956605, job 95312557582): shard timings within the same run scale with contention, not just case count (A 374.28s vs local ~102-140s, D 227.24s vs local ~32-68s). Projected shard E (local timing >= shard A's local timing in two independent measurements) anywhere from ~62% of budget (if it tracks A's real multiplier) up to over-budget (if it tracks D's or old-C's higher observed multipliers) -- genuinely uncertain, not merely tight. Unhappy-path (Gate 4, same round) independently corroborated and extended this: found the Windows CI leg already has a proven --num-processes 2 concurrency throttle (via with-test-slot.sh) that the Linux leg lacks -- built for a different contention axis (cross-job DRAM/disk/Defender) but structurally available as a cheap Linux lever if needed. Operator was presented with three options (push-as-is-and-watch / serialize pg shards via is_parallel:false / file deeper infra fix as follow-up only) via AskUserQuestion and explicitly chose push-as-is-and-watch. [disposition context: operator explicit decision, recorded via AskUserQuestion: push as-is and watch the next real CI run; --num-processes throttle on Linux and per-shard Postgres instances are both viable next levers, in that order of cost, if shard E or C is still tight/over budget]
trigger: pg shard E (and/or C) running on the Linux self-hosted (Big Tam) pool under contention comparable to the two prior TIMEOUTs on this same underlying problem
classification_rationale: engineering-velocity/CI-reliability impact only; no production system, customer, or SLO affected; not a policy floor (the Linux leg was already broken by the pre-existing problem this diff is fixing, not newly broken by this diff)
provenance: pre-existing (the single-shared-Postgres-per-runner architecture predates this branch; this diff reduces per-shard tail latency but does not resize the aggregate load)
adjudicated_by: Dave (operator, explicit AskUserQuestion decision: push as-is and watch real CI rather than act further now)
adjudication_rationale: explicit choice among three presented options: push-as-is-and-watch vs. is_parallel:false serialization vs. file-follow-up-only; chose push-as-is-and-watch

summary: flake-retry.py has no automated check for duplicate test() entry names or the pairwise-non-substring property its own match_suite() longest-substring logic relies on -- only a hand-maintained code comment. Demonstrated empirically: meson silently accepts duplicate test() names with no warning; match_suite's tie-break on equal-length matches silently keeps whichever entry was seen first. This exact class of collision already happened same-day in this PR's own history (an independent colleague PR, #3169, picked the same 'shard D' letter for unrelated content, caught only by manual git-log archaeology, not by any automated check). [disposition context: not yet filed as a GitHub issue, pending operator go-ahead; suggested fix: add a duplicate-name and pairwise-non-substring check to flake-retry.py's own _selftest(), which already parses every test() entry]

line: 'When adding a new [pg] store tag' recipe; partition-identity comments; substring-uniqueness enumeration
summary: The pre-existing recipe text for adding a new [pg] store tag ('measure it, put it in whichever of B/D is lighter by TIME, AND add it to shard C's exclusion list') and the symbolic partition-identity/naming-enumeration comments were not updated to mention shard E. Followed literally, a future tag added to D/C without also updating shard E's 22 per-clause exclusion suffixes would cause any case carrying both the new tag and one of E's 22 category tags to match D's new clause AND an E clause simultaneously -- a silent double-run, exactly the failure mode this file's own header comment says the sharding guarantees against. No effect on the CURRENT partition (independently verified zero-overlap/zero-gap by consistency-auditor, happy-path, and build-ci all separately). [disposition context: folded into amended commit -- recipe now explicitly names shard E and its 22-clause exclusion-suffix requirement; partition-identity comment and substring-uniqueness enumeration both updated to include E]
trigger: a future PR adding a new [pg] store tag to shard D/C by following the literal (stale) recipe text, without independently realizing shard E also needs the same exclusion
classification_rationale: documentation/recipe gap with a concrete future double-run consequence if followed literally -- self-correcting only if the next author independently re-derives the partition via --list-tests the way every prior rebalance in this file's history did
